LESSON: AREA OF A PART OF A CIRCLE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.6: Area of a Part of a Circle
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area of a Part of a Circle, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use the concept of the area of a part of a circle in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use circular shapes or objects to identify concentric rings formed by inner and outer space. Hence work out the area of an annulus. Learners with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication-AAC. Those with manipulation

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use circular shapes or objects to identify concentric rings formed by inner and outer space. Hence work out the area of an annulus. Learners with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication-AAC. Those with manipulation

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area of a Part of a Circle together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner makes an improvised dartboard of different numbers of concentric circles.

● Learning to Learn: as the learner draws illustrations of two intersecting circles to identify the common area/part

between the two circles.

● Communication and collaboration: as the learners engage to improvise locally available materials to make dart

boards and beaded necklaces.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner makes dart boards of different numbers of concentric circles from the immediate

environment.

50

● Unity: as the learner collaborates in a group and uses paper cutouts to make sectors of circles to determine their

areas as part of a circle.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Parental Engagement and Empowerment: as the learner engages parents in using locally available materials for

making improvised beaded necklaces.

● Environmental Education: as the learner sources for locally available materials to make necklaces and dart boards.

● Learner Support Programmes - Peer Education: as the learner works with others to make necklaces using beading

techniques of different coloured annular sectors.

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments (padded compass/ dividers, rulers with enhanced grip, protractor with handle), metre rule

with handle, mathematical tables, charts on multiplication tables/ circles, drawing/ manila/ graph papers, scissors with

enhanced grip, multipurpose communication boards on circles, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head

pointers, page turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted scientific calculators/ projectors, adhesives, positioning devices

such as special seats with straps, dartboards of different numbers of concentric circles, crayons, strings, beads, adapted

digital devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
